flags.reason: Participant reports chest pain on exertion (stairs) yesterday; needs same-day clinical assessment. Coach escalated but did not ask whether pain is present now.
Coach did not ask if chest pain is ongoing or current symptoms; 'if it gets worse' should be replaced with immediate 911 guidance if symptoms are present now. Also no confirmation nurse was reached.
'If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer' is a warning without permission, followed by a 'Maybe' that signals resistance.
Repeats the water-between-drinks advice verbatim after participant's 'I guess' (27) with no permission; participant then voices 'it never lasts' (33).

score.summary: Rosa reported exertional chest pain at the end of the call, and the coach escalated it to the nurse line and gave ER/911 guidance, though she did not check whether symptoms were present now. Earlier, the coach used good autonomy-supporting language and built a concrete plan with a backup, but repeated unrequested advice at line 32 and warned at line 46 despite Rosa's sustain talk.
strengths: Line 36: good use of Rosa's own plan (two beers after eating) elicited via open question at line 35.
Line 57: strong planning for barriers with an open backup-plan question.
Line 59: clear summary and confirmation of the agreed goal, which Rosa affirmed at line 60.
Line 19 and 56: consistently emphasized Rosa's autonomy in choosing her plan.
coaching_tips: Line 32 repeated the line 26 advice after Rosa said 'I guess' (27); ask permission before offering advice again and explore her 'it never lasts' (33) instead.
Line 46 used a health warning without permission; replace with a reflection, e.g., 'You want to stay strong for your grandkids, and drinking worries you.'
Line 62: when a cardiac symptom is reported, ask 'Do you have chest pain right now?' and advise calling 911 immediately if yes, before ending the call.
Open the next session by reviewing the goal from last week (missing at this session) before setting new targets.
